newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to tell Belgium to reclaim state aid to exporters.
newsitem.headline: EU to tell Belgium to reclaim state aid to exporters.

text.p: The Belgian government must reclaim 11.4 billion Belgian francs ($353.6 million) of illegal state aid it paid to exporting companies, European Union Competition Commissioner Karel van Miert said on Tuesday.
"Tomorrow the European Commission will formally decide that Maribel II and Maribel III have broken EU rules on state aid," Van Miert told a news conference.
"This is illegal help that must be reclaimed," he said, adding that the illegal aid totalled 11.4 billion francs.

Under the so-called Maribel II and Maribel III schemes which begun 1983 and ended in mid-1996, labour intensive Belgian firms facing foreign competition got exemptions on social security contributions ranging from 25,000 to 37,200 francs per year per worker.

Van Miert said because small firms with less than 20 employees would fall below the regulatory threshhold of 100,000 European currency units (four million Belgian francs) over a three-year period, the full amount of aid that was paid out might not be reclaimed.
"(Aid to these small firms) would have no influence on intra-Community trade," he said.
Van Miert said the Belgian government now had two months in which to reply to the European Commission's ruling.
He declined to say by when the aid would have to be repaid.
The Commissioner declined to say which individual companies would be most affected, but indicated that large firms would have to repay more than 75,000 francs per worker.
Van Miert said the European Union had no objection to general measures to fight unemployment but that they could not be targeted at exporting firms only.
Asked if the Commission would take Belgium to the European Court of Justice if the government did not comply, van Miert said: "Before going to court we will see how the Belgian government reacts".
